chapters.heading: UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE REFORM AND ACCOUNTABILITY

sections.heading: Complaints, discipline, and internal review
paragraphs: (a) The Chief shall maintain a process for receiving, reviewing, investigating, and resolving complaints against officers, special officers, employees, and personnel acting under the authority of the Capitol Police.

(b) A complaint may be submitted by a Member of Congress, officer of Congress, congressional employee, witness, invited guest, visitor, person removed from the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, person detained or arrested by the Capitol Police, or any other person directly affected by the conduct of the Capitol Police.

(c) A complaint may concern misconduct, excessive force, unlawful detention, improper arrest, abuse of authority, political bias, discrimination, retaliation, failure to follow lawful orders, improper denial of access, improper removal, neglect of duty, failure to protect, misuse of information, or any other violation of law, regulation, policy, or duty.

(d) The complaint process shall allow complaints to be submitted to the Capitol Police, the Chief, the Board, the House Sergeant at Arms, the Senate Sergeant at Arms, or any office designated by regulation to receive such complaints.

(e) A complaint concerning a House-controlled area, House proceeding, Member of the House, officer of the House, House employee, House witness, or invited guest of the House shall be notified to the House Sergeant at Arms as soon as practicable.

(f) A complaint concerning a Senate-controlled area, Senate proceeding, Senator, officer of the Senate, Senate employee, Senate witness, or invited guest of the Senate shall be notified to the Senate Sergeant at Arms as soon as practicable.

(g) A complaint concerning a shared congressional area, outside deployment, interagency operation, use of force, arrest, detention, special officer, or major security incident shall be noticed to the Chief and the Board as soon as practicable.

(h) The Chief shall ensure that each complaint is reviewed in a fair, timely, and documented manner. The review shall determine whether the complaint should be dismissed, informally resolved, referred for supervision or retraining, referred for internal investigation, referred for discipline, referred to the Board, or referred to another lawful authority.

(i) A complaint shall not be dismissed solely because the person filing the complaint is not a Member of Congress, is not an employee of Congress, was removed from the Capitol, was arrested or detained, or is unpopular with any officer, party, faction, or official.

(j) The Chief may impose discipline on officers and employees of the Capitol Police consistent with this Act, regulations issued under this Act, and generally applicable personnel rules. Discipline may include counseling, retraining, reprimand, reassignment, suspension, limitation of authority, removal from assignment, termination, referral for prosecution, or any other lawful corrective action.

(k) The Chief may suspend or limit the authority of an officer while a complaint, investigation, disciplinary matter, use-of-force review, or other serious matter is pending where continued full authority would present a risk to persons, property, proceedings, evidence, discipline, public trust, or the orderly operation of the Capitol Police.

(l) The Board may review any complaint, investigation, disciplinary action, or failure to discipline involving death, serious bodily injury, use of force against a Member of Congress, arrest or detention of a Member of Congress, interference with a congressional proceeding, political misuse, executive interference, repeated misconduct, or a substantial question concerning the lawful operation of the Capitol Police. (m)The Board may direct the Chief to reopen, continue, expand, or refer a complaint or investigation where the Board determines that the matter was not adequately reviewed, involved a conflict of interest, affected the rights or safety of either House, or raised a serious question under this Act.

(n) No officer, employee, special officer, or person acting under the authority of the Capitol Police may retaliate against any person for submitting a complaint, cooperating with a review, providing testimony, preserving evidence, reporting misconduct, or refusing to carry out an unlawful order.

(o) The Chief shall maintain records of complaints, investigations, findings, discipline, corrective action, referrals, and final dispositions. Such records shall include the nature of the complaint, the personnel involved, the location of the incident, the action taken, and whether the complaint involved force, arrest, detention, removal, access denial, political bias, or a congressional proceeding.

(p) Records concerning complaints and discipline may be maintained in closed form where disclosure would reveal personnel information, sensitive security information, classified information, private personal information, or information concerning an active investigation. Such records shall remain available for lawful review by the Board and by any committee or officer authorized by either House.

(q) The Chief shall include a summary of complaints, findings, discipline, corrective action, and unresolved misconduct issues in the report required under this Act, except that identifying information may be withheld or submitted in a closed annex where necessary to protect privacy, safety, security, or an active investigation.

sections.heading: Access rules and restricted areas
paragraphs: (a) The Chief may issue regulations governing access to the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, subject to this Act, the rules of either House, lawful orders of either House, and the authority of the Speaker, President pro tempore, Presiding Officer, and Sergeant at Arms of the relevant House over that House’s controlled spaces.

(b) Access regulations may provide for public entrances, staff entrances, Member entrances, visitor screening, identification requirements, credentialing, escorts, restricted corridors, secured rooms, gallery access, committee room access, chamber access, emergency closures, and other measures necessary to protect Congress and preserve order.

(c) The Capitol Police may deny entry to a person who refuses lawful screening, lacks required authorization, presents a security threat, attempts to bring prohibited items into a secured area, violates access rules, refuses to identify themselves where identification is lawfully required, or seeks entry into an area where access is restricted by law, rule, order, or security regulation.

(d) The Capitol Police may remove a person from a restricted area where the person is unlawfully present, exceeds the scope of their authorization, refuses to comply with lawful directions, interferes with congressional business, creates a security risk, or remains after authorization to be present has expired or been revoked.

(e) Access to the floor of the House of Representatives, the floor of the Senate, chamber lobbies, cloakrooms, galleries, committee rooms during closed proceedings, secured offices, and any other restricted area shall be governed by the rules and lawful orders of the relevant House.

(f) The Chief may designate temporary restricted areas where necessary to protect a congressional proceeding, respond to a threat, secure an emergency scene, protect a Member of Congress, protect an officer of Congress, conduct a protective operation, manage a major event, or prevent obstruction of official congressional business.

(g) A temporary restricted area shall be limited in scope and duration to the security need that justified the restriction. The Chief shall ensure that affected officers are informed of the boundaries, purpose, duration, and access rules for the restricted area.

(h) Where a temporary restricted area affects a House-controlled area, the House Sergeant at Arms shall be notified as soon as practicable. Where a temporary restricted area affects a Senate-controlled area, the Senate Sergeant at Arms shall be notified as soon as practicable. Where a temporary restricted area affects both Houses, a joint session, or a shared congressional area, the Board shall be notified as soon as practicable.

(i) The Capitol Police may establish screening checkpoints, barricades, credential stations, identification posts, access lists, secure perimeters, and controlled entry points where reasonably necessary to protect persons, property, proceedings, or facilities.

(j) Access rules shall be enforced in a neutral and uniform manner. No person may be denied entry, removed, delayed, screened differently, or subjected to a different access rule for the purpose of favoring or disfavoring any political party, faction, Member of Congress, officer of Congress, witness, nominee, ideology, viewpoint, or lawful legislative position.

(k) A Member of Congress shall not be denied access to the chamber, floor, vote, or official proceeding of that Member’s House except as provided by the rules of that House or where immediate action is necessary to prevent death, serious bodily injury, active violence, or a direct threat to the safety of persons present.

(l) The Chief shall maintain procedures to ensure that officers assigned to entrances, galleries, chambers, committee rooms, secured offices, and restricted areas understand the applicable access rules and the lawful authority controlling each space.
